audit.whatIsWrong: Level 3 and Levels 4-5 were marked Skill in both layers while the page's own whys[2] and whys[3] say Bonesaw plus passive regen out-grind you through exactly those levels.
audit.why: Infected Bonesaw is a 4-second, zero-mana, current-HP-scaling poke against the biggest HP bar in the lane, and his passive regen heals back what your chip does. The packet chart and the mirror audit both place those two stages with Dr. Mundo.
audit.corrected: win[2], win[3], phases[2].side and phases[3].side flipped to Dr. Mundo as one atomic group with ratings dropped to 4/10, and both whys rewritten to state the reason.

audit.why: Level 6 as a coin flip on whether Maximum Dosage (120s flat) is up, first item as his peak, and the 2-item drain-tank window are all accurate and already on the page; spikes[0..3] cover level 1, 6, first item and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important interaction in this matchup was absent: Dr. Mundo's passive resists the first immobilizing effect that hits him, so Body Slam's stun is simply blocked while his cannister is up. The page instead told you to track Heart Zapper generically.
audit.why: Gragas's entire all-in is built on landing the E stun; against a full-passive Mundo the stun does nothing and you have burned a 14-second dash into his face. He drops the cannister on resist and can walk over it to heal and shorten the passive's cooldown, so the correct play is to make him spend it before committing.
audit.corrected: tldr, cooldown block, report[5], dosFull[0].d and both trade lines now name the passive-vs-Body-Slam interaction and key the commit to the cannister being spent.

audit.why: All three flagged suspectNames — Infected Bonesaw and Explosive Cask — are the real Riot names for those slots. False positives.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Dr. Mundo must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: His 4s Bonesaw plus passive regen grind your HP faster than Happy Hour restores it while your cooldowns are long.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Heart Zapper's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Percent-HP Bonesaw shreds your big HP bar and his passive regen heals it back, so he out-sustains every extended trade here.

edits.before: Anti-heal him — E-Q burst chunks his HP before his regen. Gragas wins by trading around Dr. Mundo's Heart Zapper and cashing the pattern: anti-heal and burst his HP with E-Q.
edits.after: Anti-heal him and burst before the regen — but his passive eats your first stun, so make him spend that cannister before Body Slam is worth anything in an all-in.

edits.before: - Dr. Mundo Heart Zapper: matchup-defining — His sustain spike + reset. Burst when it’s down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Dr. Mundo passive: it eats your first immobilizing effect, so Body Slam's stun does nothing until he has spent it — bait it first. - Heart Zapper: 17s sustain burst. - Your Body Slam: 14s. - Explosive Cask: 100s.

edits.before: Track Dr. Mundo's Heart Zapper: His sustain spike + reset. Burst when it’s down. When it is down — E-Q burst him.
edits.after: Dr. Mundo's passive resists your first immobilize: Body Slam's stun is blocked until he spends it, so bait it out first.

edits.before: His sustain spike + reset. Burst when it’s down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: His passive eats your first stun, so make him spend it before you commit Body Slam.

edits.before: Q-poke Dr. Mundo on cooldown from fog angles, W as he answers, and E-slam only when his key tool is down.
edits.after: Q-poke Dr. Mundo from fog angles, W as he answers, and E-slam only after his passive cannister is spent.

edits.before: Body-slamming INTO his answer — a whiffed E is 13 seconds of being a barrel with no plan.
edits.after: Body-slamming a full-passive Mundo — the stun is eaten and your E is gone for 14 seconds.
